We first review the fermionic sector. Throughout this section the electron
Green's function is built from fermionic Matsubara frequencies, and all
propagators in Sec.~2 are understood in the fermionic sense unless stated
otherwise. The reader should keep in mind that every sum below inherits this
fermionic convention from the single-particle formalism developed above,
since the low-energy theory is entirely built on fermionic quasiparticles
occupying a fermionic band structure with a fermionic density of states.
Having fixed the fermionic language, we now turn to the pair susceptibility,
which is naturally expressed as a sum over the frequencies $\Omega_m =
2\pi m T$ that enter the two-particle propagator:

\begin{equation}
T\sum_{m} \frac{1}{(i\Omega_m)^2 - \epsilon^2} = -\frac{1}{2\epsilon}\left(1 + 2 nB(\epsilon)\right)
\end{equation}
